title: Model Coexistence Cartography: Experimental Plan to Quantify Interop, Latency, and Fallback Costs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Objective: Produce an evidence-backed playbook and a small instrumentation suite that quantifies how different open and third-party model variants coexist in production workloads across regions. The goal is to measure interoperability (API/behavioral drift), end-to-end latency delta, and the real customer cost of fallback policies (model substitution) so PM/Eng can set provable routing and rollout defaults for Redwood’s hosted and Dedicated offerings.

Background: Sales and SREs are increasingly asking for a defensible way to tell customers: ‘If we fallback from model A→model B (regionally or for capacity), what will you actually experience — latency change, token-cost variance, and likelihood of semantic regression on common prompt families?’ There are many ad-hoc experiments in Field Labs and ML research notes; this ticket consolidates those into a reproducible set of probes, metrics and an operational dashboard.

Key outcomes:
- Data artifact: a 12-week probe dataset that pairs identical synthetic+seeded customer prompts across 6 model variants and 3 regions with token-level timing, token pricing, and output similarity scores.
- Playbook: deterministic decision rules for routing fallback (latency-first vs cost-first vs quality-first) with concrete threshold numbers.
- Dashboard: console view prototype that surfaces per-model substitution impact (percentile latency lift, cost delta per 1k requests, quality regression rate by prompt family).
- Actionable recommendations for default rollout policy templates (e.g., prefer low-latency variant for small-context RAG; prefer lower-cost quantized variant for high-throughput batch endpoints).

Proposed experiments:
1) Controlled synthetic workload: 10k prompts sampled across 5 prompt families (short chat, code completion, summarization, embeddings-proxy, structured extraction). Run each prompt against models: M-open-alpha, M-open-beta-quant, M-vendor-x, M-redwood-tuned, M-fallback-cpu in regions us-west, eu-central, ap-south. Capture: request/response timestamps, token counts, billing unit estimation, model confidence/metadata, and deterministic seeds.
2) Real customer-shaped workload: lightweight replay of anonymized traffic (with opt-in customers) for 48-hour windows, focusing on peak and off-peak.
3) A/B failover simulations: inject capacity drain on primary model and route traffic to fallback variants under both gradual and abrupt failover. Measure user visible SLA metrics and model-output deltas.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Latency: 95th percentile per-token latency delta <= X ms for acceptable fallback; threshold numbers to be derived but target < 40ms for low-latency tiers.
- Quality: semantic drift measured via pairwise embedding cosine + task-specific scorers; acceptable fallback drift rate <= 6% regressions on critical prompt families.
- Cost: per-request token cost change reported and normalized; decision rule must show whether fallback reduces or increases unit economics per 1k requests.
- Operational: experiment runs repeatable, dataset and scripts stored in the probe repo, dashboard MVP live in Console staging.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Week 1–2: final experiment spec, instrumentation shim (ENG), and synthetic prompt bank (PM+Research).
- Week 3: controlled synthetic runs across regions; initial analysis and dashboard wireframe.
- Week 4–5: real-traffic replays (customer opt-in), A/B failover sims.
- Week 6: final analysis, playbook, handoff to SRE/Docs.

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha), Eng (Liam, Priya S.), Research (Marco L.), SRE (Dana R.), Console UX (Marta F.), Sales SME (Carlos V.).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Privacy: can we replay customer traffic without leaking PII? (Answer: opt-in customers only + inline anonymization; SRE review required).
- Modeling of quality: which task scorers are authoritative? Research recommends combining embedding-similarity with small task-specific classifiers to avoid false positives.
- Measurement noise: cross-region noise may dominate small deltas — need multiple runs and bootstrapped confidence intervals.

Dependencies: ["ENG-6723", "PM-314159", "RESEARCH-88"]

Acceptance criteria:
- Experiment repo with reproducible runbook and scripts in GitHub, linked from ticket.
- Staging Console tile showing substitution impact for at least two prompt families.
- Playbook with explicit numeric thresholds and recommended default routing for Hosted and Dedicated tiers.

Notes on uniqueness: This ticket focuses on co-existence: not just which models are better, but how substitutions affect production SLAs and unit economics across regions. That lens is different from single-model benchmarking and from model-scouting work.
